Added custom Background Color, Border Color, Corner Radius (0–28 px), Dialog Position (Auto, Corners, Edges, or Screen Center), and Custom Static Image / Animated GIF Background support (up to 25 MB, auto-scaled, adjustable opacity).
  • Classic-Friendly Default & Optional Compact Mini-Pill (360px): Enabled Classic-Friendly Mode by default to preserve Win + R → Enter muscle memory (pre-filled last command, full Browse/Run/Exit/Settings buttons, and 20-item history), with a one-click toggle to switch to Compact Mini-Pill Mode (360px).
  • Task Manager Support, Pinning, Aliases & Safe Elevation: Extended the modern UI to Task Manager → "Run new task" (Taskmgr.exe) while respecting Task Manager's own elevation checkbox (including for google: and Shift + Enter terminal launches).   • Visual & Z-Order Bug Fixes (#7600): Fixed the black bar glitch when opening/closing via Win + R (DWM cloak/transition handling) and resolved taskbar overlap via taskbar-aware work-area clamping.
  • Streamlined UX, Security & Stability Improvements: Added percentage (%) support to the instant calculator, capped stored history at 20 items for lower memory usage, removed the built-in Google Translate (文A) mode to keep the launcher focused, removed -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for elevated .ps1 execution, dropped shared #32770 class icon overrides, and hardened uninit/cleanup paths.

entry.title: Language Cursor 1.0.0
entry.content:
Language Cursor

Shows the current keyboard layout as a small badge next to the mouse pointer, so you know which language you are about to type in before you press a key. It follows the layout of the app you are working in.

Indicator modes

  • Label next to pointer: a floating badge that follows the mouse pointer.
  • Label inside text cursor: the label is drawn into the I-beam pointer that Windows shows over text fields. This replaces the system I-beam pointer while the mod is running.
  • Off: no badge. Custom pointers per language still apply.

When the badge is shown

  • Always.
  • Only over text fields: while the pointer is an I-beam.
  • Briefly after switching language: for a duration you choose.

With Show at the text caret while typing turned on, the badge moves next to the text caret when you start typing, and goes back to the mouse pointer when you move the mouse. This works in apps that report where their caret is.

It can also hide when the pointer is hidden and in full-screen apps. You can set its position around the pointer, distance, font size, opacity, corner roundness and drop shadow.

Caps Lock and Num Lock

The label can also show a mark while a lock key is on: ⇪ for Caps Lock and # for Num Lock. Each one has its own setting. The marks are part of the text label, so they aren't shown on badges that use an image.

Per-language styles

Add one entry per keyboard layout under Languages. Each entry can set:

  • a label of up to 6 characters (by default the language code, such as EN);
  • a background color as hex RGB, such as #FFB900;
  • an image shown in place of the label (PNG, JPG, BMP or GIF, first frame);
  • a custom mouse pointer (CUR or ANI) used while that layout is active.

The layout is identified by its locale, such as uk-UA, en-US, en-GB or pl-PL, or by its HKL value as 8 or 16 hex digits. Layouts without an entry get an automatic label and color. Paths may contain environment variables such as %USERPROFILE%, and the files must stay available.

Custom pointers and safety

Custom pointers and the text-cursor mode change the Windows system pointers. The mod restores the Windows pointer scheme when it is disabled or unloaded, and on its next start if it was closed unexpectedly while pointers were changed. To restore them by hand, open Windows Mouse settings > Pointers and click Apply.

Restoring reloads the whole Windows pointer scheme, so pointers that another mod or app changed at run time are reset too.

Performance

The mod runs in its own windhawk.exe process, not inside Explorer or other apps, and installs no hooks. It checks the pointer 60 times a second only while the badge is visible and the pointer is moving, and slows down to about 8 checks a second when nothing is happening. While the badge sits at the text caret, the mod also asks the app you are typing in for its caret position 8 to 20 times a second.

Limitations

  • The badge isn't shown over the secure desktop (UAC prompts, lock screen), and may not appear over some full-screen games.
  • Animated GIF images show only their first frame.
  • Showing the badge at the text caret depends on the app. Some apps don't report the caret position, and there the badge stays with the mouse pointer.
  • Only over text fields and the text-cursor mode work with the standard Windows I-beam pointer. Apps that draw their own text pointer are not detected.
  • The label I-beam in text-cursor mode is always black and white. It does not follow a custom pointer color or scheme.

entry.title: Mac-style Text Navigation 0.1
entry.content:
Mac-style Text Navigation

Makes the modifier keys behave like on macOS when moving the text cursor: Ctrl acts like Cmd and Alt acts like Option.

Shortcut Does the same as (Windows) macOS equivalent
Ctrl + ← Home (start of line) Cmd + ←
Ctrl + → End (end of line) Cmd + →
Alt + ← Ctrl + ← (previous word) Option + ←
Alt + → Ctrl + → (next word) Option + →

Holding Shift as well extends the selection, as expected.

Notes

  • The mod runs in a dedicated background windhawk.exe process and uses a global low-level keyboard hook, so it works in every application.
  • The remapping applies everywhere, not only in text fields. For example, Alt+Left/Right no longer go Back/Forward in browsers, File Explorer and Settings, and Ctrl+Left/Right lose app-specific meanings (such as jumping to the edge of a data region in Excel). Use the "Excluded programs" setting for apps where you want the original behavior.
  • Windows running as administrator are not affected unless Windhawk itself runs elevated (a Windows security restriction).
  • Ctrl+Alt combinations (including AltGr) and combinations with the Win key are left untouched.
  • Modifiers produced by remapping tools that inject input (e.g. PowerToys Keyboard Manager, AutoHotkey) are not recognized. Remaps done through the scancode map (e.g. SharpKeys) work.

entry.title: Ookla Speed Test for Network Menu 1.0
entry.content:
Ookla Speed Test for Network Menu

Right-clicking the network icon in the Windows 11 taskbar and choosing Run internet speed test normally opens a web page in your browser. This mod replaces it with a native flyout above the taskbar that runs the official Ookla Speedtest CLI in the background and shows the test live.

Screenshots

Download Upload History

Features

  • Live gauge (0 to 2,000+ Mbps) drawn as a soft light bar with smooth motion: blue for download, purple for upload.
  • Ping, jitter, download and upload measured by Ookla. The server is always picked automatically.
  • Test history: when a test finishes, the flyout moves to a list of the last 100 tests (date and time, IP, server, download, upload, ping) with the new test on top. Click a row to open its result page on speedtest.net.
  • Copy puts the result, including the speedtest.net link, on the clipboard.
  • Follows the Windows light/dark theme, transparency, DPI and the "Animation effects" setting. Keyboard (Tab, arrows, Enter, Esc) and screen reader accessible.
  • Interface in English or Portuguese, following the Windows display language.

Requirements

  1. Download the Speedtest CLI for Windows from speedtest.net/apps/cli and extract speedtest.exe.
  2. Put it at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\speedtest\speedtest.exe (the default), or set its path in the mod settings.

Ookla license and privacy

Before the first test, the flyout explains what Ookla receives and links Ookla's EULA, Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. No test runs until you click Accept and test. Only then does the mod start speedtest.exe with --accept-license --accept-gdpr. The acceptance is stored separately for each Windows user.

The Speedtest CLI also records the acceptance in its own file, %APPDATA%\Ookla\Speedtest CLI\speedtest-cli.ini, which stays after the mod is removed. Delete that folder to reset it.

Network access

The mod opens no connections itself. It runs speedtest.exe, which:

  • contacts Ookla's servers to pick a test server, then downloads from and uploads to that Speedtest server;
  • uploads the result to speedtest.net, where Ookla stores it (the result link in the history points there).

Ookla receives your public IP address, your internet provider and the test results, under its privacy policy.

A test runs every time the flyout opens, and on Start, Repeat or Retry. Set Start the test automatically to Never to make tests click-only (Auto already waits for a click on metered connections). Clicking a history row or a terms link opens speedtest.net in your browser.

Data usage

Ookla does not cap a test: on a 2 Gbps line one test moves about 4-5 GB. With Start the test automatically set to Auto, the flyout waits for a click when Windows reports the connection as metered.

Notes

  • Stop, Esc, closing the flyout or disabling the mod ends speedtest.exe immediately (it runs inside a kill-on-close job object).
  • The history lives in the mod's own Windhawk storage, separately for each Windows user, and is removed with the mod.
  • Network Menu Speed Test intercepts the same link. If both are installed, disable one of them.

Credits

Based on Network Menu Speed Test by Alessandro-Vecchio, which provides the hooks and the original flyout. This mod swaps its Cloudflare engine for the Ookla Speedtest CLI and adds the light bar, the smooth motion and the test history.

entry.title: Volu - macOS Volume HUD 1.0.0
entry.content:
Volu - macOS Volume HUD

Authentic macOS-style translucent volume HUD for Windows with classic step click sounds.

Features

  • Pixel-perfect design: Authentic macOS frosted glass HUD overlay with clean 16-step volume bar and soft drop shadow.
  • Audio feedback: Classic wooden and modern tactile volume step clicks. Silent on mute.
  • Smooth animations: Smooth fade-out transition with configurable on-screen duration.
  • Flexible positioning: Place the HUD at the center, top, or bottom of your screen.
  • Optional hotkeys: Global shortcuts (Ctrl + Alt + Up, Ctrl + Alt + Down, Ctrl + Alt + V), disabled by default to avoid shortcut conflicts.
  • Native flyout suppression: Intercepts physical media keys (Volume Up, Volume Down, Mute) system-wide using RegisterHotKey, suppressing the default Windows flyouts.
  • 1/16 Quantization: Each key press changes volume by 1/16 (6.25%) matching macOS, instead of Windows' default 2%.
  • Dynamic device switching: Automatically follows the default audio output device when headphones, speakers, or Bluetooth devices are connected.

Key Capture & Shortcuts

The mod captures physical volume keys system-wide via RegisterHotKey, so other apps no longer receive the volume keys:

  • Volume Up — Increase volume by 6.25% (1 step)
  • Volume Down — Decrease volume by 6.25% (1 step)
  • Volume Mute — Toggle mute

Optional shortcuts (if enabled in settings):

  • Ctrl + Alt + Up — Volume Up
  • Ctrl + Alt + Down — Volume Down
  • Ctrl + Alt + V — Mute / Unmute

Comparison with Other OSD Mods

Unlike win10-volume-brightness-osd (which restores Windows 8/10 flyouts with brightness controls) or osd-custom-pill (which provides modern animated pills), Volu is focused exclusively on authentic macOS volume HUD fidelity:

  • Classic square frosted glass aesthetics with multi-pass soft drop shadow.
  • Authentic wooden and tactile step clicks.
  • 16-step quantization (6.25% per step) strictly synchronizing with the 16-segment bar.
  • Lightweight tool mod architecture dedicated solely to volume control.

entry.title: Sharp Taskbar Icons After Remote Desktop 1.0
entry.content:
Sharp Taskbar Icons After Remote Desktop

Connecting with Remote Desktop from a device with a different display scale (for example the Microsoft Remote Desktop app on a phone, at 200–300%) switches the session to that scale, and Explorer renders the tray icons for it. When you come back to the local screen, Explorer doesn't render them again from the programs' icons — it rescales the copies it already made, so they stay blurry until the program or Explorer is restarted.

This mod asks Explorer to render the icons again. For the tray it uses the copy of each icon that Explorer itself keeps for the tray button; as a fallback (for icons it can't find there), it remembers the icon each program gives the tray, by watching the WM_COPYDATA messages that Shell_NotifyIcon sends to the taskbar and Explorer's answers to them. When the session returns to the local console, it waits until the scale has stayed the same for a few seconds (Explorer may pass through an intermediate scale, and turns tray requests down while it rebuilds the taskbar) and then:

  • asks Explorer to render every tray icon again (NIM_MODIFY with the icon Explorer itself keeps for that tray button, or the program's own icon handle for icons that aren't in the tray toolbars — what happens when the program is restarted, but without restarting anything). Explorer's copy is used because many programs destroy the handle they give the tray right after giving it;
  • asks the taskbar to re-read the icon of every top-level window (HSHELL_REDRAW through the taskbar's shell hook message). Buttons of pinned programs that aren't running are not refreshed.

If Explorer turns most tray icons down because it is still busy, or the scale changes again, the tray is refreshed again (for about a minute after returning).

While the remote session is active, the mod checks the taskbar's scale every few seconds. If it never differed from the local screen's scale, nothing is done. The Windhawk log shows the scales and how many icons were refreshed.

Icons that existed before the mod was enabled are handled too: their copies are read from the tray at refresh time. The exception is an icon a program registered by GUID before the mod was loaded: Explorer only accepts it by its GUID, which the mod learns when the program registers or updates the icon. Nothing is sent to other programs.

Made for the Windows 10 taskbar (tested on Windows 10 22H2), and for Windows 11 versions whose taskbar still behaves like it; not tested on the newer Windows 11 taskbar. The newer Windows 11 (XAML) notification area has no tray toolbars, so there only icons registered while the mod was running are refreshed.

entry.title: ZoneShift - Per-App Timezone Spoofer 1.0.0
entry.content:
ZoneShift - Per-App Timezone Spoofer

ZoneShift is a lightweight, high-performance Windhawk mod that spoofs the time zone and local time for individual Windows applications without changing the system clock or affecting other running programs.

Why Per-App Timezone Spoofing?

  1. Wallpaper Engine & Desktop Customization:

    • Web wallpapers (Chromium/CEF), Scene wallpapers (DirectX/native), and Edge wallpapers can display the local clock of any chosen city (e.g. Tokyo, London, New York) or simulate day/night lighting cycles for a different hemisphere without altering your PC's real clock.

  2. International Outreach & Client Work:

    • Localize browser profiles, CRM tools, scheduling calendars, Slack, Discord, or web apps to match client timezones, avoiding timezone math errors while keeping your taskbar clock accurate.

  3. Software Testing & QA:

    • Verify application behavior across global regions (e.g., date-boundary logic, DST shifts, calendar schedulers, daily reset intervals) on demand.

  4. Privacy & Anti-Fingerprinting:

    • Mask your real physical timezone from web tracking scripts and telemetry engines that cross-check timezone offsets.

Important Usage Notes

  • Adding Custom Applications: By default, ZoneShift targets Wallpaper Engine processes to keep other apps unaffected out of the box. To target any other application (browsers, chat apps, games, etc.):

    1. Open the Windhawk UI.
    2. Navigate to ZoneShift -> Details -> Advanced tab.
    3. Under Process inclusion list, add the executable name (e.g., chrome.exe, slack.exe, yourapp.exe).
    4. Click Save.

  • Web Wallpapers and Time Shifting: Chromium/CEF web wallpapers evaluate local time via ICU using the spoofed TimeZoneKeyName and UTC time. To apply an artificial minute offset in web wallpapers, enable Shift UTC Time.

  • UTC Time Shifting in Browsers: Enabling Shift UTC Time shifts GetSystemTime. Note that shifting UTC time by more than a few minutes in web browsers may cause HTTPS security certificate validation failures, expired cookies, or invalid TOTP two-factor authentication codes. Keep this option disabled unless specifically required.

  • Client Games & Anti-Cheat: Many multiplayer games employ anti-cheat systems that inspect or block process hooks. Use caution when injecting mods into protected games, and note that server-authoritative games determine daily resets on the game server.

How It Works

Windows apps query time through multiple Win32, NT, ICU, CRT, and registry APIs. ZoneShift intercepts all critical layers at the process level:

  • GetDynamicTimeZoneInformation & GetTimeZoneInformation: Modern Win32 APIs used by Chromium, Electron, CEF, Node.js, and ICU to resolve IANA and Windows timezones.
  • GetLocalTime: Native API called by C++/DirectX apps, desktop widgets, and Wallpaper Engine scene wallpapers.
  • SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTime[Ex] / TzSpecificLocalTimeToSystemTime[Ex]: Local-to-UTC and UTC-to-local conversions with full dynamic Daylight Saving Time (DST) support.
  • FileTimeToLocalFileTime / LocalFileTimeToFileTime: File and timestamp conversions.
  • NtQuerySystemInformation (SystemTimeOfDayInformation): Low-level NT kernel time-of-day bias.
  • RegQueryValueExW: Intercepts TimeZoneKeyName and ActiveTimeBias queries.
  • Windows ICU Integration: Automatically converts any IANA identifier (e.g. Europe/Warsaw, America/Mexico_City, Asia/Tokyo) to Windows time zones using icu.dll.

Source Code & Support

Source code, issue tracker, and documentation: GitHub Repository

entry.title: Quick Share Tile 1.0.0
entry.content:
Quick Share Tile

Replace the Windows 11 Nearby sharing Quick Settings tile with a Quick Share launcher.

Keep your Quick Settings layout intact while giving the native Nearby sharing tile a new purpose.

Preview

Features

  • Replaces the Nearby sharing tile with Quick Share.
  • Changes the tile's name and icon.
  • Preserves native tile dimensions, position and styling.
  • Launches Quick Share with a single click.
  • Automatically restores the original tile when disabled.

Requirements

  • Windows 11 x64, build 24H2 or later (Quick Settings hosted by ShellHost.exe).

  • Windhawk.

  • Google's Quick Share for Windows installed (not Samsung's app of the same name).

  • Quick Share shortcut located at:

    C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Quick Share.lnk

Settings

Native tile to replace

The accessibility name of the tile to replace.

Default: Nearby sharing

The name is language-dependent. Change it if your Windows installation uses another display language.

Log the visual tree

Logs the Quick Settings visual tree for troubleshooting.

Known Limitations

  • Tested on Windows 11 x64 build 26300.
  • Other Windows builds are not guaranteed to work.
  • The tile's active appearance still reflects Nearby sharing, not Quick Share's actual running state.
  • The Quick Share shortcut path is currently hardcoded.
  • This mod launches Quick Share; it does not implement Quick Share functionality.

Credits

Parts of the ControlCenter.dll hooking and cleanup logic are based on refined-quick-settings-and-sound (GPL-3.0-only). This mod is therefore also released under GPL-3.0-only.

Uninstallation

Disable or remove the mod through Windhawk.

The original Nearby sharing tile is restored, including its label, icon, click behavior and keyboard navigation.

entry.title: System Tray BreakTimer 0.1.8
entry.content:
System Tray BreakTimer

Each time you enable the mod, it starts paused. Click P in the notification area to start. Windows can place new icons in the tray overflow.

S means Standby until the next whole clock minute. A fresh interval started at exactly :00 begins immediately. With the default 15-minute interval, starting at 1:01:25 shows S until 1:02:00. The tray shows 2 at 1:15:59, then 60 in the seconds color at 1:16:00. It counts down to 1 in seconds. Set Start seconds countdown to any value from 5 to 60 seconds. For example, at 10 seconds the tray shows 1 minute until 1:16:50. The break starts at 1:17:00 and lasts one minute by default. B means a break is in progress. Hover over the icon for the unit, time remaining and pause reason. Both minutes and seconds use bold numerals in your chosen tray colors.

The borderless break window has a Skip Break button and a gauge-colored X in its upper-right corner. Both end the break silently and start a fresh work interval with the usual Standby. The gauge scales to 90% of the shorter usable monitor dimension. With multiple windows, one action applies to them all. To skip with the keyboard, Alt+Tab to the break window marked B and press Enter on Skip Break.

Tray commands

A single left-click toggles pause. Pausing discards the current interval, and unpausing starts a fresh one. Turn on Require a double-click to pause or unpause if you prefer. Keyboard activation still takes one press. Right-click the tray icon to open its menu.

When the tray shows P, the menu contains only Unpause. During S / Standby or B / On break, the menu contains only Pause. During the work countdown, including its final seconds, the menu has three commands.

  • Skip to next break starts a break immediately. Its end schedules a fresh work interval.
  • Reset ends the current phase and starts a fresh work interval.
  • Pause discards the current countdown, closes any break windows and leaves the mod paused indefinitely until you unpause it. When you unpause, S appears until the next whole minute, then the entire Break every interval begins. At exactly :00 it starts immediately.

Sound — In Settings, Play wind chimes is on by default. The default audio device plays one short chime for each of these two events.

  • The tray countdown reaches zero and a scheduled break begins.
  • The gauge reaches 00:00 and the break finishes naturally.

Choosing Skip to next break starts the break silently. It still chimes if the gauge reaches zero. Skip Break, X, Reset, Pause and Unpause are silent. Each event plays its cue once across all monitors. Turning sound off also stops a cue already playing.

The bundled wind chime was recorded by GnoteSoundz and is available under CC0 1.0. To use your own recording, browse to a local WAV under Custom sound file (optional). Choose uncompressed 8- or 16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, at 8–48 kHz, up to 10 seconds and 2 MiB. An empty field or an unreadable or unsupported file uses the bundled chime. On Windhawk 1.x, you can paste a quoted path copied from Explorer. If you replace the WAV at the same path, switch sound off and back on to load it again.

Settings — Open the mod's Details, then Settings. Windhawk 2.0 alpha 8 shows break durations as minute sliders and includes a file browser. Windhawk 1.x uses numeric fields for durations and a text field for the WAV path. If Break every is below twice Break for, the timer uses twice the break length. For example, a 25-minute break and a 40-minute interval give 50 minutes of work. Changes to durations apply on the next fresh interval or break. Appearance changes take effect immediately. Set Background opacity under Tray icon to 0% for a transparent background or to 100% for a solid color. After an update, the saved opacity slider value controls the background. Windows controls whether the full-screen pause banner appears. The timer pauses independently of banner delivery.

Automatic pauses

After five idle minutes during work or Standby, the icon shows P. The timer starts a fresh Break every interval when you return. Ordinary idle time during a break lets the gauge run to zero.

Locking or disconnecting the session, suspending the PC, or entering full screen with auto-pause enabled also pauses the timer. If a break is in progress, its window closes silently. When the last pause reason clears, the icon shows S until the next whole minute, then starts the full work interval. At exactly :00 it starts immediately. For example, unlocking at 2:04:20 starts the default 15-minute work interval at 2:05, with the next break at 2:20.

A manual pause lasts until you choose Unpause. Choosing Unpause also overrides a current idle or full-screen pause. An unavailable Windows session must reconnect, unlock or wake before a new interval can begin.

Full-screen auto-pause and its optional banner both default to off. With auto-pause off, the break window can appear over a game or presentation and may interrupt exclusive full screen. Enable Auto-pause for full-screen apps to pause the timer while a full-screen app is detected.

Inspired by Stretchly. Functionality inspiration only. No code was reused.

entry.title: Snap Groups: Alt+Tab and taskbar 0.5.3
entry.content:
Snap Groups: Alt+Tab and taskbar

Keep native Snap Groups in Alt+Tab and give each group a separate taskbar button with a grid of its application icons. Individual member buttons can be hidden; windows outside groups remain accessible.

Usage

Enable Snap windows and the option to show snapped groups in Alt+Tab under Windows Settings > System > Multitasking. Arrange at least two windows into a native Snap Group. The mod reads groups maintained by Windows.

A group button brings all members forward. With the default click setting, clicking an active group minimizes it. If a member is already minimized, the button restores the group. Closing a group button minimizes the group by default and does not close the applications. Group buttons are temporary and cannot be pinned; ordinary pinned application launchers remain.

The taskbar label uses the native localized group title. Hover previews use the Windows group visual. Win+Tab is unchanged. Group commands use native Windows activation/minimization; animation behavior follows those native commands.

Settings

  • Independently enable Alt+Tab filtering, group taskbar buttons and hiding of individual member buttons.
  • Keep separate buttons for separate groups, including groups of the same apps.
  • Display two to four equally sized icons in a two-column grid. Adjust icon size, spacing and incomplete-row alignment. The icon limit does not limit membership.
  • Order icons by screen rows from top to bottom and centers from left to right. A tall window belongs to its first row (default), or use Windows' member order. Minimized windows use restored positions; only icon order changes.
  • Choose restore-only or minimize-if-active behavior, and the close-button action.
  • Adjust refresh interval and current-virtual-desktop filtering.
  • Enable or disable native hover previews.
  • Diagnostic mode keeps individual Alt+Tab cards and disables taskbar integration.

Tested configuration and limitations

Version 0.5.2 was tested on Windows 11 25H2 (26200.8246, x64), Windhawk 1.7.3: Alt+Tab advancement, group activity and no empty buttons after disable/enable; group recovery, native previews, Alt+Tab/activity and minimize/restore after Explorer restart; group creation on the other monitor. Separate classic/modern preview routes were not independently identified. The support-trace toggle and heavy-game scenario below were confirmed on 0.4.24, not repeated for 0.5.x.

  • Independent taskbar per monitor 1.7.0: group creation, moving groups between monitors and restoring minimized groups; no empty buttons or unload stalls in the tested disable/enable scenario.
  • Alt+Tab per monitor 1.2.1: switching during a heavy game and after closing it, including disabling both mods without restarting Explorer.

Taskbar integration calls native DLL methods and COM interfaces; it does not parse machine instructions or read private task-list/preview object fields. Native task items come from the shell enumerator. Hidden members and pending button restores use owned window icons until their own task list is restored. Native previews replace the window thumbnail factory for owned group proxies; Windows creates and manages the visual itself. Required shell symbols must be available. Missing optional preview/selection methods leave those paths native. Shell interfaces are undocumented; other Windows versions and DLL revisions remain unverified, and updates can require changes to the mod. Longer sessions and other monitor/DPI/virtual desktop configurations have limited coverage. ARM64 installation is allowed; ARM64 runtime behavior is unverified.

Report mod problems in https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/issues. Include "hide-snapped" in the title and mention @coldfeudal in the report.

Diagnostics and removal

Windhawk debug logging records phase codes and counts without window/document titles. Disable this mod to restore the native taskbar and switcher behavior. Enable Record support trace only when collecting diagnostics. Changing this setting reloads the mod. Bounded journals are stored in Windhawk's per-mod storage directory, in the traces subfolder. A background writer saves queued records. Records may be dropped under load. Journals contain numeric identities, counts and stack/module information, without window titles or AppID strings.

The Alt+Tab scoping approach was informed by Alt+Tab per monitor.

entry.title: Floating Taskbar 2.1.15
entry.content:
• Pass a valid timer handle to CreateTimerQueueTimer during the initial taskbar layout calibration.
  • Skip applying the floating taskbar until TaskbarFrame is loaded and has an XamlRoot.
  • Harden Explorer restart initialization against invalid timer output and pre-load taskbar application.

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 1.3.0
entry.content:
• Write in your own language. The bar takes input from the Windows language bar and its input method, so Chinese, Japanese, Korean and every other IME work: type the reading, see the composition underlined in the search field with the candidate list under the caret, and the characters you pick land in the search. Nothing is searched until you accept a candidate, and the text goes into the field you are editing - the search, the path bar, a custom entry or the entry manager.
  • The Windows key as the shortcut. Pick Win under Shortcuts and pressing the Windows key opens the bar. The Windows Start menu is kept closed so only one panel appears; the candidate list, the result list and the rest of the bar work the same as with any other shortcut.
  • Shortcut help follows the setting. The F1 sheet and the settings page show the Windows key as the shortcut when that is what you picked.
